quandoUsar: Photo gallery (product, travel, portfolio, attachments) where the user opens an image, zooms in, and moves to the neighboring ones.
When opening the image should preserve the sense of place: the thumbnail grows into the image and returns to the same spot on close.
Images with a short caption that call for zoom by mouse wheel, pinch, double click, or keyboard.
quandoEvitar: Use `carousel` to move through slides within the page itself, without opening a full-screen layer.
Use `image-compare` to compare two versions of the same image.
Use `infinite-masonry` for a long feed of varying heights that loads more on scroll; here the grid has fixed columns and mounts all thumbnails.

teclado.acao: On a thumbnail, open the viewer on that image.
Go to the previous or next image; with `loop`, wrap at the ends.
Go to the first and last image.
Zoom in and out in 1.6× steps, up to `maxZoom`; `=` also zooms in and `0` returns to the fitted size.
Closes the viewer: the image returns to the thumbnail and so does focus.
Cycle through the viewer's controls (zoom, close, arrows, thumbnail strip) without leaving it.

acessibilidade: The viewer is a Radix dialog: it traps focus, closes with `Esc`, and on close returns focus to the thumbnail of the last image viewed.
Each thumbnail is a button with `aria-label` “Open image N of M: alt”, and the `aria-live` counter announces the current image on each change.
Provide `alt` on all images (it names the buttons and is read in the counter) and `label` for the gallery; the control labels are hardcoded in English.
movimento: The pressed thumbnail grows on a spring to the size fitted to the screen and returns faster on close; if it is offscreen, the image only fades.
Between images, the new one enters from the side of the movement; the drag follows the finger, resists when there is nowhere to go, and switches images past the threshold or on a fling.
With “reduced motion”, opening, closing, and switching become a fade, and zoom by button or key jumps straight to the level.
responsivo: The grid always keeps `columns` columns (3 by default), with no breakpoints: adjust the prop according to the available width.
Below 640 px the side arrows disappear and navigation is by swipe and the thumbnail strip, which scrolls horizontally; the image's side margins drop from 84 px to 12 px.
desempenho: Grid thumbnails use `loading="lazy"`; pass `thumbnail` with a smaller file, which also serves as a preview while the full image loads.
Provide `width` and `height` so the viewer knows the aspect before loading; the thumbnail strip mounts all images at once, so very large galleries are heavy.
notasIA: The component renders the grid and the viewer: pass `images` with `src` and `alt`, and preferably `thumbnail`, `width`, `height`, and `caption`.
`value` is the index of the open image or `null` (closed): control it with `onValueChange`, which receives the index on open or switch and `null` on close, or use `defaultValue`.
The viewer opens in a full-screen portal (`position: fixed`, `z-index` 80 and 81); `className` applies only to the thumbnail grid.
